12 Pre-Cut Mini Treats Dessert Fun Kids Sewing Kit for Kids Ages 8-12 Children Beginners Sewing kit kid crafts Make Your Own Felt Pillow Plush Craft Kit Girls and Boys Art Craft Kits Learn to Sew Kit I do not show where this item is made. . . But. . . I know it’s not made in the USA. How do I know that? Because though the listing pictures show a box that has “Dessert Sewing Kit” on it. . . .The actual box I received shows “Desert Sewing Kit”. So I can only assume this item is Made in China and that they didn’t have a native English speaker check the spelling.

You’ll find some super simple “sewing kits” for sell on Amazon. This one is not it. It’s certainly not super complicated, but there are different stitches / needles used. Blanket stitch. . .Whip stich. . . .Running stitch. The box shows from ages 8 and up. I think even at the age of 8; adult supervision will be needed.

There are indeed twelve projects included. An instruction booklet is included and instructions given for each project. The set comes in a cardboard box measuring 8.75” X 6” X 2.75”. Easy to wrap, if you’re giving as a gift.

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide The 3Doodler Create + is both a toy and an artist's tool. While trying it out the hours flew by, I felt like a little kid playing with new toys on Christmas morning. Despite the fact that it will take a lot of practice before I can make anything useful or artistic, I'm having a blast trying to learn how to make various shapes. The instructions are very basic, but the website has lots of hints, tips, projects, and stencils to download for free. There are quite a few YouTube videos as well.

As the packaging states, the tip gets incredibly hot. However, the pen's design makes holding it and using it comfortable without risk of a burn. There are 2 types of filaments in the kit; ABS and PLA.

PLA is made from sugarcane and cornstarch and is used for plastic cups, cutlery, and other food grade plasticware. It has a lower melting point and a slightly glossier finish but is not as strong as ABS.

ABS requires a higher melting point and has a chemical smell but it is stronger and less likely to break if dropped.

Cleaning it after use is easy. If there is still some of the plastic sticking out from the unheated end of the pen you simply tap one of the speed buttons twice and it goes in reverse. Once the filament clears the gear mechanism, which can be seen through a clear window, it's easy to pull out. If there is no plastic sticking out then simply use the rest of it up or the long tool can be used to push the remainder out once the tip is removed. The kit has tools to accomplish this and more. The website has good visual instruction for removing the plastic.

So far I wrote my dog's name. The second try was legible but more practice is needed. I then made a pyramid. Not too difficult but a bit rough...more practice needed. I have tried to make a long vertical spiral...haven't figured that out yet. I think it's best if I stick with 2 dimensional objects until I am better able to control the pen and it's flow. Once I master that - look out! I'd like to make a small lampshade, Christmas ornaments, and focal beads for jewelry.

Just what I need, another hobby!!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide

Learning Resources Slam Ships Sight Words Game - Ages 5+ Educational and Fun Games for Kids, Board Games for Kids, Kindergarten Games I love this game for my children. It's a great way to help in getting some of the words to stick into their minds that they've had a harder time keeping there. My favorite part is the fact that the cards are double sided and color coded. Level one cards are blue(pre-primer), level two is red(primer), level three is green(first grade), level four is orange(second grade), and level five is purple(third grade). There are four different colored spaceships and they stick to the cards with suction. The cards are made of thick cardboard, and while they do look nice and well made, the suction is so great that sometimes it can bend the cards trying to pull the spaceship off. On those, it's best to pull up on the side of the spaceship a bit(like with a fingernail) to release the suction.

The game can be played with multiple children, as a competition, but for now I've only did one child at a time, working on one level at a time, too. The child picks up the cards he knows first, which goes into the "know" pile(and then we don't work on those again unless it's for review). I then call out a word at a time of what's left and he figures out the word from there. We do this until all the words are in the "know" pile(through different days) and then move to the next level. We've enjoyed having it around as another option to help with sight words.

Castle Panic 2nd Edition | Family Board Game | Board Game for Adults and Family | Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ | for 1 to 6 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Fireside Games I purchased this game with the intention of playing with my 5 year old daughter, wife, and possibly my 4 year old son. This has proven to be a great game. I don't think most avid gamers would find it as fun, simply because the design is you play against random board mechanics. Some real bad draws and no matter how good you are, you just can't beat it. Other times, it's skill and other times it's just luck of the draw.

That said, this game is EXCELLENT! There's no heavy competition (unless you use some of the modified rules). Basically, everyone WINS or everyone LOSES. That means my daughter's not nagging her brother, etc, etc. It's a great family game for this reason where it is cooperative. The theme is also the fun part, while you're playing, you will have nail biting times, and easier times, etc. We just purchased it and have played it over 5 times in the last week. My nephews have come over and played multiple times too. It's also great because it can host up to 6 players, which is excellent!

The only downfall I've seen is this. Avid gamers might not like it as it's light in strategy, meaning it's easy to play (almost self guided at times). Also, this game can be harder to play at certain player numbers. For example: 2 players each player has 6 cards, and that's 12 total to look at. With 5 players, there's 5 x 5 hands meaning 25 cards making the odds alot better. Basically 2 and 3 player games can be rough. Lower player games aren't unwinnable, it's just higher difficulty (which again is mostly random). Out of 5 stars I definitely rate this a 4. i would give it a 5 if it wasn't so random (meaning hopeless on some games). By the way, out of 5 games played, we've won 4...so it's not 'that' hopless really...great game!!!
text_fidelity_b: Castle Panic 2nd Edition | Family Board Game | Board Game for Adults and Family | Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ | for 1 to 6 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Fireside Games

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448) So....I'm Gen X and we played the original version some in college along with games like Risk and Stratego on weekends. It isnt quite a fluff game but it isnt very hard. I would think both children and adults would enjoy this game. A game adults can enjoy with their kids....or a fun starter game or game for chatting and having a beverage or three.

The best part is there is hardly any explanation needed to get started. Move tiles to open a path to get to the objects on your cards. And....block others from their goals. I love this game especially with 3 or 4 people instead of two. It requires some strategy but luck can make or break it, too.

Harry Potter version! Yes! Well...it is beautiful. The board looks wonderful! But in this version you are gathering "people" or characters rather than treasure items. The premise makes sense. Going through the maze that is Hogwarts gathering people ....you must match cards in your hands to pics on the tiles of the gameboard. Sounds AWESOME. In reality...it is kind of messy because some people look similar. Some people are the big characters...such as Harry or Snape....there were 3 I was like....who on earth is THIS and I thought I was a big fan. So....due to the pics on the game board being rather small....they are also color coded too. If your card is Harry with a blue border....Harry has a blue border on the game tile as well. But is there another character who looks very similar on the board with a blue border? Yes there is. So....yeah, it is really cool BUT pay good attention as the character pictures certainly are NOT as easy to discern as a scarab or diamond in the original. Hey...but it looks great!

I give this game 10 out of 10 because my gripes do not effect the game. If you are are a HP fan....and you already like or think you might like a labyrinth game...here ya go. This is 100% Ravensburg quality. The box is good quality as all the pieces. The box holds everything in the usual labyrinth organized way. Very nice.

At the price point....I really, really, really dont like wooden pegs. They are sort of big, bright and easy to move but I liked the Labyrinth version with the plastic characters NOT the one with wooden pegs. I have no idea WHY if your player piece coincides with a house....such as Slytherin....they didnt atleast make little plastic coats of armor for each house. I just hate generic pegs in fun games. But it doesnt make the game any better or worse. I saw some reviews where people complained about the card quality. It is the same it always has been. The cards are simply there to identify your next goal. This game doesnt require shuffling like Uno or slapping...or grabbing or swapping cards. They are perfectly fine.

Great game. Great Ravensburger quality. Dear Ravensburger.....I sure would love a Scooby Doo version with cool plastic player pieces!

I included pics and pics of game pieces from an earlier version of the original game
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448)

text_fidelity_a:
Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

Ravensburger Neuschwanstein Castle 2000 Piece Panorama XXL Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly For the last 15 years my extended family has been assembling puzzles during our beach vacation at the North Carolina Outer Banks. We now have a well established family tradition of puzzling with increasingly challenging puzzles. For the last few years, only Ravensburgers will do. These puzzles are well made, with thick, solid cardboard with a bright, spill resistant color.

The difficult part about this puzzle are the vast blue and cloudy blue areas at the top, and the large amounts of snow covered tree limbs. At 132 cm wide, this puzzle is 4' 4" across, much wider than most coffee tables. We set up a specific rectangular folding table for puzzles like this, or push two together. I would judge this puzzle as on the "difficult" end for puzzles with 2,000 pieces (to be precise, it has 2,040 pieces!). It took our family a full week to work through all the branches, blues, snow, etc.

A nice thing about this puzzle is that even though its 2,000 pieces, the pieces are all a "large" nice size, which makes it more fun, and easier to tell one from another, and spot tiny differences in color and shape.

The insert in the box comes in a wide variety of languages, the pieces come inside the sturdy box wrapped in a bag. Its quality throughout.

Have fun!

text_fidelity_a:
Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In We've been playing with Vector for a little over a month now, and he's a load of fun! At first, he didn't do a lot, but every so often, Anki provides an update and suddenly, Vector has more personality, skills, and interactions! He's a great little desk companion that is much better than a pet because there's little to clean up afterward! I say little because he's been known to shove things off the table!
There are many ways he can learn about his environment via his sensors:
He sees via HD camera.
Facial recognition - he'll learn your face and when he's exploring, will come right up, scan your face, and say your name! He's very pleased when he recognizes you, and gets a little upset if he doesn't recognize you.
Navigate, explore, and learn his environment. He gets around very well all over my desk. However, I move things a lot, so he's constantly having to re-learn. Occasionally, he'll fall over the edge, but once in a while, he falls over the edge. I think they're working on improving that a lot. It's super cute when he's exploring, gets close to the edge, and acts scared and backs away!
If he needs charging, he'll go right back to his charger on his own. However, sometimes, I'll get tired of hearing him causing trouble, so I'll tell him to go to his charger. He does it, but throws a little tantrum when he gets there!

He can hear via his array of four microphones. Sometimes he comes over to see what's going on if you're having a conversation. If he's resting, he'll act startled if there's a loud noise in the room. He will also react to the beat of music if it's loud and near him. If you ask him to look at you or come here, he'll be able to sense the direction to go.

He reacts to touch and feel. If you pet his back, he practically purrs! But shaking him gets a reaction, too!

He has amazing intelligence. For instance, he answers questions, plays blackjack, reacts to his environment, and senses actions and activities around him.

He speaks to you. I'm not a fan of his synthesized voice, but it seems to be improving. When he reads out answers to questions you ask, sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. However, as they receive feedback on this, I'm sure his voice will evolve into something more understandable.

We really enjoy seeing his reactions! The current one is the way he gets super excited when you tell him he's a good robot or if you tell him you love him, and pouts a little if you tell him he's a bad robot! I just told him earlier today when he picked up his cube and tossed it off the desk!

I'm super excited to see his ever-evolving skills! I highly recommend this little guy for your favorite tech lover, or yourself! If you're looking for a toy for younger kids, maybe go with a Cosmo. This doesn't have games or things to entertain little ones. But it's completely entertaining for maybe, 10 years and up robotics fans!
text_fidelity_b: Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In

text_fidelity_a: Kamigami Scarrax Robot - Discontinued by Manufacturer This box weighs next to nothing, and the contents are not particularly impressive when you open the box -- causing me to raise an eyebrow at what seems like a high price.  But after putting this toy together, you realize that you are not paying for the physical materials that make the toy, but rather for the programming that makes the toy fun.  In the box, you will find a flat plastic sheet stamped with eight parts, a bag of teeny-tinyplastic rivets for assembly, a USB charger cable, and some electronic body parts.  It takes a little bit of patience (and steady fingers) to put this the Scarrax together, but it is not particularly difficult, and no special tools are required.  It's mostly a matter of folding the pieces from the plastic sheet and snapping them together with the rivets.  I would allow an hour, at least, for getting everything together.  Once assembled, you can download the app on an apple or android device, and program your robot to do whatever.  Scarrax can really more -- you'd be surprised at his speed and dancing ability, particularly considering he's made from a single flat sheet of plastic.  I would say this is appropriate for late tweens and teens, although some younger children might be able to use it (1) if they're super geniuses or (2) with adult help.
text_fidelity_b: Kamigami Scarrax Robot - Discontinued by Manufacturer

Highlights Hidden Pictures Search Game and Book Love this for my toddler! This comes with two items - a hidden flashlight game and a activity book. The two are independent, so I will review them independently.

The hidden flashlight game is so cool. This one is a 4 paneled game where you stick flashlights into either side's opening and then try to find hidden objects. You can do an "easy mode" or a "hard mode" - the difference is that one type of flashlight illuminates the whole "path" of its light, while the other just has a small "spotlight" circle. At some point, if you play this thing enough, you'll probably memorize where everything is, but they claim 1,000+ different items, so it should be a long while until that happens.

The activity book is nice too, though not atypical of other similar activity books. It's got your expected mix of coloring, connect the dots, spot the differences, etc. But it's a thick and meaty book so would be great for long car trips or dinners. I wish the quality of the pages were a little higher, as ours is already getting abused, but again - not atypical of these kinds of books.

All in all, a great package for some good dedicated board game nights or long trips.

They're simple enough that you could easily draw it off on a piece of paper real quick or you could copy several and have them ready in the box ahead of time.) It's perfect for those rough, stress filled days.

Within this kit, you get a storage box that doubles as an easel. The 10 activities are attached to the box by a spirally bound book. Each of the activities are on both sides of the page, so that children can sit on each side of it and still be able to see. It also comes with 2 cups, 4 double sided dry erase boards, 4 dry erase markers, 20 number cards, 40 frog counters(double sided: red on one side, yellow on the other), and a guide(which contains 2 reproducible worksheets).

If your child could use extra practice with adding and subtrating numbers 1-20, this is a nice kit to try.

It looks good, has a smooth ride, with a snazzy traditional bell to alert the neighbors.That's all good, but it needs more work at the design level.

The handlebars don't seem to attach securely, but not unsafely. A 3 year-old might not be able to loosen them, but any adult certainly can. Tighten them as hard as you can.

The cover for the handlebars -- where it attaches to the headset (just above the wheel) pops off whenever the wheel is turned. It is intended to, and does, snap in when still, but should remain snapped in always.

This book, on my opinion, is most beneficial for children 1-3 years of age. Very impressive

In summary, this book is well worth the money. It develops and reinforces counting skills, builds vocabulary and teaches children in an engaging way with visual and tactic appeal. Great job Melissa and Doug!

All the features like follow me and point of interest work as expected I have yet too use way points on any of my birds, but the WiFi connection and FPV work well too.
